messages.author: fdaa54d30ab7b913
messages.subject: Question about predict for a model with 2 factors
parts:
Dear list members,

I have an occupancy model with 2 factors (f1 and f2) for occupancy ("state").  The model is additive (not interaction).
Each factor has 3 levels and I am expecting to have 6 estimates (3 for each factor) based on the model that I fitted (best model in my set of candidate models).

When I use predict I got 9 estimates (each combination of the levels factors).

 > newData  <-  expand.grid(f1 = c("a", "b", "c"), f2 = c("a", "b", "c"))
> newData
      f1    f2
1    a      a
2    b      a
3    c      a
4    a      b
5    b      b
6    c      b
7    a      c
8    b      c
9    c      c

> predict(mod5brid,  type  =  "state",  newdata  =  newData,  appendData  =  TRUE)
   Predicted         SE      lower     upper f1 f2
1 0.27010704 0.10251099 0.11782446 0.5062587    a      a
2 0.60022605 0.11270967 0.37420667 0.7903483    b      a
3 0.78911719 0.08551492 0.57747872 0.9110718    c      a
4 0.05085778 0.03158974 0.01464119 0.1619373    a      b
5 0.17857399 0.07975317 0.06967606 0.3868906    b      b
6 0.35141307 0.11329031 0.16979955 0.5893747    c      b
7 0.17690344 0.08032784 0.06794318 0.3878837    a      c
8 0.46580773 0.11468941 0.26108134 0.6827395    b      c
9 0.68486537 0.10457781 0.45673910 0.8488901    c      c

How can I get only the 6 estimates (3 for each factor, because I do not have interaction)?

Thank you very much in advance.

Best,

Manuel

messages.author: 9548b9e0c8258268
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Question about predict for a model with 2 factors
parts:
Manuel,

Even though there is no interaction, there are still 9 possible predicted values.  Since there is no interaction, these 9 predicted values each are a sum of only two estimates.  Predict is just adding the estimates as you would expect from the newData object that you printed.  So all is well there.

I have a feeling that what you want is more like a marginal prediction (like SAS's LSMEANS), where you get the predicted value for each level of one factor, averaged over the levels of the other factor (see for example http://www.uiweb.uidaho.edu/ag/statprog/sas/workshops/glm/handout2.1_glm.pdf).  You would need to compute these manually since unmarked/R doesn't have an LSMEANS equivalent that I'm aware of.  You might make use of unmarked's linearComb method to help you out.

Ian

 if what you need are the LSMEANS equivalent, then isn't that computed as follows, e.g., for f1=a, the estimated effect is just the average of the 3 effects for f1=a:
 (.27 + .05 + .18)/3
do this for each value of f1 averaged over all levels of f2 and then for each value of f2 averaged over all values of f1.

messages.author: 9548b9e0c8258268
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Question about predict for a model with 2 factors
parts:
Hi Manuel,

Andy is exactly right -- this will give you the point estimates for the LSMEANS.  And if you additionally want to get the standard errors, then linearComb will provide this for you.  To help you figure out the coefficients to use with linearComb, here's a small reproducible example using lm (since this is an R modeling issue rather than an unmarked issue).

data <- data.frame(f1 = gl(3, 3, 27, c("a", "b", "c")),
                   f2 = gl(3, 1, 27,  c("a", "b", "c")),
                   y = rnorm(27))
fm <- lm(y ~ f1 + f2, data)
coef(fm)
(Intercept)         f1b         f1c         f2b         f2c 
 0.06979306 -0.18754312  0.56563158 -0.46392095 -0.26595500 

Then, you would get your LSMEANS with the following 6 vectors. 

f1,f2, coefficients
a, .:  1,0,0,1/3,1/3
b, .:  1,1,0,1/3,1/3
c, .:  1,0,1,1/3,1/3
., a:  1,1/3,1/3,0,0
., b:  1,1/3,1/3,1,0
., c:  1,1/3,1/3,0,1

You can make these into a single matrix and pass it to linearComb.

Hope that helps,
Ian

To have the estimate for f1-a I do:

linearComb(mod5brid, coefficients = c(1, 0, 0, 1/3, 1/3), type = "det")

for f1-b:

linearComb(mod5brid, coefficients = c(1, 1, 0, 1/3, 1/3), type = "det")

for f1-c

linearComb(mod5brid, coefficients = c(1, 0, 1, 1/3, 1/3), type = "det")

for f2-a

linearComb(mod5brid, coefficients = c(1, 1/3, 1/3, 0, 0), type = "det")

for f2-b

linearComb(mod5brid, coefficients = c(1, 1/3, 1/3, 1, 0), type = "det")

for f2-c

linearComb(mod5brid, coefficients = c(1, 1/3, 1/3, 0, 1), type = "det")

Is that correct?

Best,

Manuel
